'''Indus Towers Limited''' is an Indian [[telecommunications]] infrastructure company offering passive [[Infrastructure as a service|infrastructure services]] to [[mobile network operator]]s and other wireless services providers. Headquartered in [[Gurugram]], [[Haryana]], Indus Towers was incorporated in November 2007 by [[Bharti Infratel]] (a subsidiary of [[Bharti Airtel]]), [[Vodafone India|Vodafone Essar]], and [[Idea Cellular]], to provide shared telecom infrastructure to telecom operators on a non-discriminatory basis.

Bharti Infratel merged with Indus Towers on 19 November 2020, creating one of the largest [[Cell site|mobile tower]] infrastructure operators in the world.<ref>{{cite news |date=20 November 2020 |title=Largest tower company in world outside China! Indus Towers, Bharti Infratel merger complete |publisher=[[Business Today (India)|Business Today]] |url=https://www.businesstoday.in/sectors/telecom/largest-tower-company-indus-towers-bharti-infratel-merger-complete/story/422492.html}}</ref> Post-merger, Bharti Airtel held a 36.73% stake in Indus Towers, with [[Vodafone|Vodafone Group Plc]] holding 28.12%,<ref name=":0" /> and 3.1% shares held by [[Providence Equity]].<ref name="shareholding" />

Currently Indus Towers is a subsidiary of Bharati Airtel after the latter increased its stake to 50.005% & Vodafone Group Plc exited the company

Indus Towers Limited has over 192,874 towers and 342,831 co-locations and a nationwide presence covering all 22 telecom circles.<ref name="livemint.com">{{cite news |last1=Guha |first1=Ishita |title=Indus Towers Q3 net profit up 2% at ₹1,360 crore |url=https://www.industowers.com/investor/company-profile/|publisher=[[Livemint]] |date=28 January 2021}}</ref> It has the widest coverage in India and has already achieved 289,000 tenancies, a first in the telecom tower industry globally.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/economy/policy/merger-to-give-vodafone-idea-more-negotiating-powers-in-divesting-indus-tower-stake/articleshow/57761645.cms|title=Merger to give Vodafone, Idea edge in divesting Indus Towers stakes|last1=Sengupta|first1=Devina|date=2017-03-22|work=The Economic Times|access-date=2017-07-25|last2=Banerjee|first2=Niharika}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/company/corporate-trends/indus-towers-to-invest-rs-100-crore-to-set-up-500-new-sites-across-india/articleshow/55683542.cms|title=Indus Towers to invest Rs 100 crore to set up 500 new sites across India|last=Aulakh|first=Gulveen|date=2016-11-29|work=The Economic Times|access-date=2017-07-25}}</ref> Some of its major customers include Airtel, Bharti Hexacom, [[Jio]] and [[Vodafone Idea Ltd|Vi]].<ref name="livemint.com" />

==History==
Indus Towers Limited was founded in November 2007 by [[Bharti Infratel]], [[Vodafone India|Vodafone Essar]], and [[Idea Cellular]], with the goal of merging their passive infrastructure assets across 16 telecom circles.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2009-11-20 |title=Indus raises Rs 10000 crore to pay off loans |work=The Economic Times |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/telecom/indus-raises-rs-10000-crore-to-pay-off-loans/articleshow/5252771.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2023-05-21 |issn=0013-0389}}</ref> It was incorporated with an objective to provide shared telecom infrastructure to telecom operators on a non-discriminatory basis.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.financialexpress.com/archive/teri-and-indus-towers-jointly-ink-mou-on-developing-innovative-renewable-energy-solutions/318567/|title=TERI and Indus Towers jointly ink MoU on developing innovative renewable energy solutions|work=The Financial Express|access-date=2017-07-25|language=en-US}}</ref> Bharti Infratel held a 42% stake in the company, with [[Vodafone|Vodafone Group Plc]] holding 42% and [[Vodafone Idea]] holding 11.15%.<ref name=":1">{{Cite news |date=2020-11-20 |title=Bharti Infratel, Indus merger complete; VIL gets ₹3,760 cr in cash for 11.15% holding in Indus |language=en-IN |work=The Hindu |url=https://www.thehindu.com/business/Industry/bharti-infratel-indus-merger-complete-vil-gets-3760-cr-in-cash-for-1115-holding-in-indus/article33138890.ece |access-date=2023-05-21 |issn=0971-751X}}</ref> The remaining 4.85% stake was held by private equity firm [[Providence Equity]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kundu |first=Navadha Pandey, Rhik |date=2018-04-25 |title=Infratel, Indus merge to form a tower giant |url=https://www.livemint.com/Industry/GwT2LjndrV3OzfTncD20nM/Bharti-Infratel-Indus-Towers-announce-merger-to-create-tele.html |access-date=2023-05-21 |website=mint |language=en}}</ref>

===Bharti Infratel merger===

In 2017, reports suggested that Bharti Infratel was looking to acquire the 53% stake in Indus Towers, owned by Vodacom Group and Vodafone Idea.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.livemint.com/Industry/PjsOVZLNNhskBfdWgEbHnK/Bharti-Infratel-said-to-sound-out-banks-to-fund-8-billion-I.html|title=Bharti Infratel said to sound out banks to fund $8 billion Indus Towers deal|last=Alexander|first=George Smith|date=2017-06-01|work=livemint.com/|access-date=2017-07-25}}</ref> However, in July, the head of Vodafone stated that they were "actively considering" a float of their stake in Indus Towers. Vodafone went on to deliver a formal mandate to both [[Bank of America Merrill Lynch]] and [[Morgan Stanley]] to finalize buyers.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/economy/policy/tower-sale-plan-of-vodafone-idea-gathers-steam-ahead-of-merger/articleshow/59394089.cms|title=Tower sale plan of Vodafone, Idea gathers steam ahead of merger|last1=Parbat|first1=Kalyan|date=2017-07-01|work=The Economic Times|access-date=2017-07-25|last2=Kalesh|first2=Baiju}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.businessinsider.in/Vodafone-India-Idea-merger-on-fast-track-Individual-towers-to-be-sold-at-the-earliest/articleshow/59399370.cms|title=Vodafone India-Idea merger on fast track: Individual towers to be sold at the earliest|work=Business Insider|access-date=2017-07-25}}</ref>

[[Bharti Airtel]] (Bharti Infratel's parent company), Vodafone Group, and Vodafone Idea announced on 25 April 2018 that they had signed an agreement to [[Mergers and acquisitions|merge]] Bharti Infratel with Indus Towers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Merger of Bharti Infratel and Indus Towers: creating a listed pan-India tower company |url=https://www.vodafone.com/news/technology-news/merger-of-bharti-infratel-and-indus-towers |access-date=2023-05-21 |website=Vodafone.com}}</ref> Under the terms of the agreement, Bharti Infratel will transfer 1,565 of its own shares for each Indus Towers share valuing the latter at $10 billion. Other major shareholders in Indus Towers such as Idea Cellular and Providence Equity Partners would be provided an option to cash out.<ref>{{cite web |title=India's Bharti Infratel, Indus merging to form $14.6 billion... |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-indus-towers-bharti-infratel/indias-bharti-infratel-indus-merging-to-form-14-6-billion-telecom-tower-giant-idUSKBN1HW0C8 |website=Reuters |access-date=29 March 2019 |language=en |date=25 April 2018}}</ref> Prior to the merger, shareholding in Indus Towers was Bharti Infratel (42%), Vodafone Group (42%), Idea Cellular (11.15%) and Providence Equity Partners (4.85%).<ref>{{cite web |last1=Sengupta |first1=Devina |title=Bharti Infratel-Indus Towers merger likely to complete in the first quarter of next fiscal |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/telecom/telecom-news/bharti-infratel-indus-towers-merger-likely-to-complete-in-the-first-quarter-of-next-fiscal/articleshow/67456706.cms |website=The Economic Times |access-date=29 March 2019 |date=9 January 2019}}</ref>

The merger was originally planned to go through before October 2019. However, due to delays in approvals, it was postponed to December 2019 by when the [[Department of Telecommunications]] (DoT) was supposed to give its permission. Owing to further delays by the DoT and the [[National Company Law Tribunal]] the deadline was extended multiple times to 24 June 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |date=10 June 2020 |title=Bharti Infratel-Indus Towers merger may finally go through: Here's what the deal could look like |url=https://www.cnbctv18.com/telecom/bharti-infratel-indus-tower-merger-may-finally-go-through-heres-what-the-deal-could-look-like-6108991.htm |access-date=1 July 2020 |website=cnbctv18.com |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Leo |first=Leroy |date=23 April 2020 |title=Lockdown delays Bharti Infratel-Indus Towers merger, deal postponed for 4th time |url=https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/lockdown-delays-bharti-infratel-indus-towers-merger-deal-postponed-for-4th-time-11587648419533.html |access-date=8 August 2020 |website=Livemint |language=en}}</ref>

The DoT approved the merger on 21 February 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-02-21 |title=DOT approves merger of Indus Towers with Bharti Infratel |url=https://www.deccanherald.com/business/business-news/dot-approves-merger-of-indus-towers-with-bharti-infratel-806888.html |access-date=2023-05-21 |website=Deccan Herald |language=en}}</ref> The merger received [[foreign direct investment]] approval and was due to be completed by 31 August.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 2020 |title=Vodafone Idea to divest stake in Indus Towers after Infratel merger |url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/companies/vodafone-idea-to-divest-stake-in-indus-towers-after-infratel-merger-5486241.html |access-date=1 July 2020 |website=Moneycontrol}}</ref> The merger was approved by Bharti Infratel's board on 1 September, and by Vodafone Group in October 2020.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2020-10-05 |title=Vodafone lenders approve merger of Indus Towers with Bharti Infratel |work=The Economic Times |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/telecom/telecom-news/vodafone-lenders-approve-merger-of-indus-towers-with-bharti-infratel/articleshow/78490553.cms |access-date=2023-05-21 |issn=0013-0389}}</ref> The merger was completed on 19 November 2020. Vodafone Idea received {{INRConvert|3760.1|c}} as cash compensation for its 11.15% stake. Post-merger, Bharti Airtel received a 36.73% stake in the merged entity and Vodafone Group held a 28.12% stake.<ref name=":0">{{cite web |date=19 November 2020 |title=Bharti Infratel, Indus Towers merger done; VIL sells Indus stake for ₹3,760 cr |url=https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/bharti-infratel-indus-towers-merger-complete-vodafone-idea-sells-indus-stake-for-rs-3-760-cr-11605806024934.html |access-date=21 May 2023 |website=mint |language=en}}</ref> The remaining shares are held by private equity firm Providence Equity Partners (3.1%) and public shares (35.2%).<ref name = "shareholding">{{Cite web |date=2020-11-19 |title=Bharti Infratel, Indus Towers complete merger process |url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/info-tech/bharti-infratel-indus-towers-complete-merger-process/article33135455.ece |access-date=2023-05-21 |website=www.thehindubusinessline.com |language=en}}</ref> The merger made Indus Towers the second largest telecom tower infrastructure operator in the world.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Gupta |first1=Deepali |last2=Barman |first2=Arijit |title=Bharti Infratel ringing in a merger with Indus to create world's largest telco |work=The Economic Times |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/stocks/news/indus-set-to-merge-with-bharti-infratel-to-create-worlds-largest-towers-co/articleshow/63904128.cms?from=mdr |access-date=23 July 2020}}</ref>

===Vodafone Group sells entire stake in Indus===

On June 19, 2024, UK's Vodafone Group Plc said that it has sold an 18% stake. Out its 21.05% holding — in Indus Towers for Rs 15,300 crore. The stake sale proceeds will be used to clear bulk of the UK company's existing lender dues relating to $1.8 billion of borrowings secured against its Indian assets.

On 5 December, Vodafone Group Plc sold the remaining 3.05% stake, permanently exiting the company. The stake sale will be used to pay $101 million owed to Indian banks and the remaining money will be used to subscribe to preferred shares of Vodafone Idea which will be used to reduce outstanding debt with Indus Towers.
